text: At half past eight that evening. <break time="0.8s" /> A young messenger came on a bicycle. <break time="0.8s" /> And dropped a note into the box. <break time="0.8s" /> In his answer. <break time="0.8s" /> Old Dorset wrote that our demands were a little too high. <break time="0.8s" /> If we brought Johnny home. <break time="0.8s" /> And paid him. <break time="0.8s" /> Two hundred and fifty dollars. <break time="0.8s" /> He would take the boy. <break time="0.8s" /> Off our hands. <break time="0.8s" /> He also told us to come at night. <break time="0.8s" /> Because his angry neighbors might hurt. <break time="0.8s" /> Anyone bringing the boy back. <break time="0.8s" /> Sam, what is two hundred and fifty dollars. <break time="0.8s" /> After all, said Bill. <break time="0.8s" /> One more night with this boy. <break time="0.8s" /> Will drive me crazy. <break time="0.8s" /> To tell the truth. <break time="0.8s" /> The boy had gotten on my nerves too. <break time="0.8s" /> So I agreed. <break time="0.8s" /> We got the boy to come home. <break time="0.8s" /> By telling him that his father had bought him a silver rifle. <break time="0.8s" /> At exactly midnight. <break time="0.8s" /> We knocked at Dorsets door. <break time="0.8s" /> And Bill counted two hundred and fifty dollars. <break time="0.8s" /> Into his hand. <break time="0.8s" /> When the boy learned. <break time="0.8s" /> That we were leaving. <break time="0.8s" /> He held Bills leg so tightly. <break time="0.8s" /> That his father had to pull him off. <break time="0.8s" /> How long can you hold him. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked Bill. <break time="0.8s" /> And Dorset said. <break time="0.8s" /> I think I can promise you ten minutes. <break time="0.8s" /> Enough, said Bill. <break time="0.8s" /> And he was a mile and a half out of Summit. <break time="0.8s" /> Before I caught up with him.
